Theme

Latin word

exemplum

exemplum, exemplī n.

noun, second declension

a copy, transcript (of a letter or text); an example, an instance; a model to follow; example (to follow or to avoid); a sample (of goods)

In this lexicon

  • copy

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Att. 8.6.1: deinde supposuit exemplum epistolae Domitiī (Lewis & Short); Traupman 28; Traupman 297

  • example

    the recommended word · classical · Cic. Phil. 13.2: exemplī causā paucōs nōmināvī; Traupman 146: exemplum praebet; Traupman 222; Traupman 311

  • model

    also used · classical · Sen. Ep. 6.5: breve et efficāx per exempla; Tac. Germ. 7.1: ducēs exemplō potius quam imperiō

  • sample

    the recommended word · classical · Auct. Her. 4.6.9: purpurae, trīticī (Lewis & Short); M-O s.v. sample (of product), after Vives

  • exemplum mittere: forward

    classical

  • exemplum phōtotypicum: photocopy

    modern
